doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Cannonball Adderley as an inspiration
summary: Cannonball Adderley's ability to paint pictures with an instrument inspired her; they note his Nancy Wilson album.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Were there horn players that inspired you from an improvisation standpoint too?

Well you know it’s interesting because the one person that comes to mind is Cannonball Adderley. You know I had the opportunity to hear him when I was really young, and I just thought he was amazing. And I think that the thing that inspired me more than anything was that he had this way of creating places and times and pictures with an instrument that had no words, but he could make you have these thoughts and feelings about places that you’ve been or places that felt very, very familiar. He gave you pictures. So I think early on he was the one. And then I loved when he worked with Nancy Wilson. I thought that was really cool.
Was that the best album ever made just about?
Yeah that was a great album.
Yeah, absolutely. And it’s funny because she says that actually the critics gave her some heat about that, or maybe him.
Oh critics give so much heat.
